Cullen Skink Chowder

Served at: St. Andrew's Day

Serves 4-6Prep 20 minCook 30 min

Cullen Skink is a classic, hearty Scottish soup originating from the town of Cullen in Moray, Scotland. This creamy, warming chowder features smoked haddock, potatoes, and onions, traditionally simmered in milk. It's a beloved comfort food, particularly cherished on St. Andrew's Day, Scotland's national day, offering a taste of Scottish culinary heritage.

Ingredients

  • 1 tablespoon (14g) unsalted butter
  • 1 medium onion, finely chopped
  • 2 medium (about 1 lb / 450g) floury potatoes, peeled and diced into 1/2-inch (1.2 cm) cubes
  • 1 pound (450g) undyed smoked haddock fillet
  • 3 cups (700ml) whole milk, plus more if needed
  • 1 cup (240ml) water
  • 1/2 cup (120ml) heavy cream
  • 1/4 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper, or to taste
  • Salt to taste (smoked haddock is salty, so taste first)
  • 2 tablespoons fresh parsley, chopped, for garnish

Method

  1. In a large pot or Dutch oven, melt the butter over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and cook gently for 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent, but not browned.
  2. Add the diced potatoes to the pot and stir to coat with the butter and onion.
  3. Place the smoked haddock fillet into the pot with the potatoes and onions. Pour in the milk and water, ensuring the fish is mostly submerged. Bring the liquid to a gentle simmer, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and cook for 10-15 minutes, or until the haddock is cooked through and the potatoes are tender.
  4. Carefully remove the cooked haddock from the pot and set it aside on a plate to cool slightly.
  5. Using a fork, flake the haddock into bite-sized pieces, checking for and discarding any skin or bones.
  6. Return the flaked haddock to the pot with the potatoes and cooking liquid. Stir in the heavy cream.
  7. Heat the chowder gently for another 2-3 minutes, stirring occasionally, until it is warmed through. Do not let it boil after adding the cream.
  8. Season the Cullen Skink with freshly ground black pepper. Taste before adding salt, as smoked haddock can be quite salty. Adjust seasoning as needed.
  9. Ladle the hot Cullen Skink into bowls and garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

Tips

  • For a thicker chowder, mash some of the cooked potatoes against the side of the pot before adding the cream.
  • Serve with crusty bread or oatcakes for dipping, a traditional accompaniment.
  • Leftovers can be stored in the refrigerator for up to 2 days and reheated gently on the stovetop.
